summary: A tower listed as Fort Mudge in Ware County, Georgia; sources cover the namesake fort and a 1955 fire nearby, but not the tower's own history.

the community is in Brantley County (so it may not be the tower's place)
evidence.quote: is an unincorporated community in Brantley County in the U.S. state of Georgia

evidence.supports: the community takes its name from the fort

notes_for_editor: The tower itself has only the tnlandforms list entry (31.07628,-82.2025; 135 ft; code gfc-836), which the record also holds as GFC US 836. Wikipedia, the Charlton page and the 1955 Georgia Forestry article are about the namesake fort and a nearby fire, not the tower; none names the lookout. The 1955 fire is therefore not logged as an event on this record. County difference (the community and the tower may not be the same place): the tower list says Ware; Wikipedia places the community in Brantley; the 1955 article puts the fire about five miles south of Waycross. The record keeps Ware and no correction is proposed, since the tower's own source says Ware. The Charlton page places Fort Mudge near Cowhouse Island, which may not be the same place as the community. The same page dates the wagon-train attack to August 1938, while its other dates are 1838, so the year is probably a typo; the story leaves the year out. Leads not read: NGS datasheet BS0012 (named in the list), Georgia Forestry Commission tower records, and later issues of Georgia Forestry. No build date, height, status or staffing found. Confidence low. The story no longer calls the community small; no source says so, and Wikipedia says it is unincorporated. The tnlandforms page does not name Tom Dunigan in the fetched text; the attribution is kept as in the other stories, unconfirmed on the page.
